item.title: Korea’s Lee Hails Trump’s ‘Determination’ for Peninsula Peace
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung lauded President Donald Trump’s push to resume dialogue with North Korea even as Pyongyang denied any top-level communication between their leaders and dismissed the US decision to scale down joint drills with South Korea.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: UK’s Miliband Plans Sanctions Over Israeli Settlement Expansion
item.description: UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the government would prepare new targeted sanctions against Israelis participating in “illegal settlement expansion” in Gaza and the West Bank, in the latest sign of Labour’s hardening stance toward the Middle East nation.
item.dc:creator: Lucy White

item.title: Democratic Socialist Wins Upset in FL Senate Primary | Balance of Power: Late Edition 08/19/2026
item.description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia says he opposes more data centers in his district, arguing that development has created power and environmental problems and driven up some residents' utility bills. Jason Furman, former Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers under President Obama, says higher interest rates are "likely here to stay" as government and businesses compete for capital, with US national debt surpassing $40 trillion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says US Starting ‘Economic Warfare’ Operation Against Iran
item.description: President Donald Trump announced plans to inflict what he called “an ECONOMIC D-DAY” against Iran, underscoring his rising frustration with the country’s refusal to capitulate despite weeks of military strikes and a US blockade that’s crimped its oil exports.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank

item.title: Higher Interest Rates Are 'Likely Here to Stay': Furman
item.description: Jason Furman, former Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers under President Obama, says higher interest rates are "likely here to stay" as government and businesses compete for capital, with US national debt surpassing $40 trillion. Furman says Congress ultimately must address the fiscal imbalance through spending cuts, tax increases, or both. He also weighs in on the economic impact of AI, arguing meaningful productivity gains may still be one to three years away as businesses learn how to deploy the technology. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Subramanyam: Data Centers Need Community Buy-In
item.description: Democratic Representative Suhas Subramanyam of Virginia says he opposes more data centers in his district, arguing that development has created power and environmental problems and driven up some residents' utility bills. Subramanyam calls for a national strategy to site data centers where sufficient power can be provided without negatively affecting surrounding communities and expresses skepticism about "bring your own power" proposals that rely on diesel backup generators. He says the US should remain a leader in AI, but communities should not have to shoulder the costs of the infrastructure needed to power it. He speaks with Kailey Leinz on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Minutes Released as Yields Continue Climb | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 8/19/2026
item.description: Bloomberg TV & Radio International Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee breaks down the minutes from the July Fed meeting, where the board splintered on whether or not to raise interest rates. BlackRock Head of US iShares Fixed Income Strategy Karen Veraa-Perry also joins Businessweek to react to headlines from the minutes. Plus, President Trump held a meeting Wednesday at the White House with top Crypto leaders. Bloomberg News Senior Executive Editor stacy-marie ishmael, White House Correspondent Jeff Mason, and Bloomberg Government Senior Capitol Hill Reporter Cristiano Lima-Strong preview the event and what it means for the Trump Administration's crypto agenda. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Set to Cut Canada Auto Tariffs to 15% in Trade Deal
item.description: The Trump administration is poised to reduce tariffs on automobiles imported from Canada to 15% from 25% as part of a broader deal that would see the US neighbor drop retaliatory trade measures, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, David Welch and Gabrielle Coppola

item.title: Anxious Manufacturers Await Canada-US Deal to Avoid 50% Tariffs
item.description: Canadian companies facing 50% tariffs on exports to the US remained in limbo as President Donald Trump delayed a deadline to finalize a deal until Friday — prolonging uncertainty weighing on Canada’s economy.
item.dc:creator: Mathieu Dion and Erik Hertzberg

item.title: Trump’s Fast-Track Presidency Hits Pause on Tariffs, Iran and DC Makeover
item.description: After racing through his second-term agenda, the president is now taking his time on his signature policies — sometimes not by choice.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Trump Says He May Lower Tariffs on Canada to Other Countries' Levels (Q&A)
item.description: President Trump told reporters that he may lower tariffs on Canada to a level consistent with other countries, after earlier Bloomberg reporting that the US is set to halve tariffs on Canadian exports of steel and aluminum. President Trump said that he has a 'very nice relationship' with Canadian leadership right now as the two countries settle on a trade deal. The president also discussed the AI industry, telling reporters that he is planning to meet with 'AI people' next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Asks Congress to Pass Crypto Bill Alongside Executives
item.description: President Donald Trump pressed Congress to pass digital asset market structure legislation that is a top priority for the industry, as he hosted cryptocurrency executives at the White House on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian and Tyler Kendall

item.title: Trump, Carney Optimistic on Trade Deal | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 8/19/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses trade negotiations between the US and Cananda. On today's show, former US Ambassador to Poland Daniel Fried, Push Digital Group Vice President T.W. Arrighi, former Obama White House Special Assistant Allison Jaslow and former New Jersey Governor Chris Christie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Voter Registration, Data 'Not a Federal Issue,' Says Former Governor Chris Christie
item.description: Former Governor of New Jersey Chris Christie said that issues around voting registration and administering elections should be left up to states and does not see evidence from recent years that the federal government would run elections better than Governors in individual states. Christie, who is now a strategic advisor to the American Gaming Association, also weighed in on prediction market regulation and said that he is glad prediction market executives were left out of a White House meeting because they are 'illegal actors.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed Minutes Show Many Officials Said Rate Hikes May Be Needed
item.description: Bloomberg's Mike McKee said that Fed minutes reflect Kevin Warsh's comment that the FOMC meeting was an 'old fashioned family fight' as members argued over inflation and the potential for a rate hike. Minutes showed that several Federal Reserve officials were in favor of an interest-rate hike last month and said that policy tightening would be necessary if inflation didn't decline. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Set to Cut Tariffs on Canada Metals, Autos in Trade Deal
item.description: The tentative trade deal between the US and Canada would lower tariffs on certain Canadian exports of steel and aluminum to 25% and cut duties on Canadian auto exports to 15%, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove, Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Alicia Diaz and David Welch

item.title: Ecuador Courts Chinese Money While Teaming Up With US Military
item.description: One of Donald Trump’s top allies in Latin America is visiting China this week, trying to secure long-term investments from the US rival.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Kueffner

item.title: North Korea Denies Kim Talks as Trump Eyes Meeting This Year
item.description: North Korea denied any direct communication between Kim Jong Un and President Donald Trump even as the US president said he’s seeking to meet with the strongman this year.
item.dc:creator: Se Young Lee and Tyler Kendall

item.title: Peltola’s Strength in Alaska Boosts Democratic Hopes for Senate
item.description: Mary Peltola’s strong showing in Alaska’s Senate primary is bolstering Democratic hopes that the party can defeat a two-term Republican incumbent — and possibly help it retake both houses of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Anna Edgerton and Derek Wallbank

item.title: Democratic Socialist Nixon Dominates Florida Senate Primary
item.description: Democratic Socialist Angie Nixon stormed to a surprise win in Florida’s US Senate primary, while Republican Representative Byron Donalds, backed by a $100 million war chest and President Donald Trump’s endorsement, cruised to victory in his gubernatorial primary.
item.dc:creator: Michael Smith, Daniel Cancel and Anna J Kaiser
